subject.title: [Feature]: Session busy status reply + cancel option during long-running model responses

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic scripted busy-reply contract for active session contention, and what default/config/action semantics should it use?
rationale: Source inspection shows the gap is real, but choosing default-on versus opt-in, text/config shape, busy reason vocabulary, and portable cancel/new-session actions is product behavior, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design the generic busy-reply contract
options.body: Add a core reply payload for active-session contention, with channel-safe action metadata and tests proving no second model run or queued-message loss.

options.title: Keep only typing/status cues
options.body: Treat the existing typing/status reaction behavior as sufficient and close or narrow this request to docs explaining queue modes and /stop.

options.title: Defer to broader status-surface work
options.body: Make this a partial overlap of the persistent long-running status surface and avoid adding a separate busy-reply contract until that design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Design the generic busy-reply contract
recommendation.body: Add a core reply payload for active-session contention, with channel-safe action metadata and tests proving no second model run or queued-message loss.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the queue-policy and busy-followup paths that would need to own the product contract.
